newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-North's Anderson sees flat Q1.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-North's Anderson sees flat Q1.

text.p: Mining and forestry group North Ltd managing director Campbell Anderson said on Wednesday he expected results for the first quarter of the 1996/97 year (July-June) to be flat.
"We will be steady, but it would be flat as expected," Anderson told Reuters, after being asked about first quarter trading.

Anderson reiterated that the results for 1996/97 year would be flat, but that he expected a rise in earnings during the 1997/98 year on the back of new projects that are expected to start over the next 18 months.

"1996/97 will be relatively flat," Anderson said, but added the following year would see a substantial profit rise due to new gold and copper projects, and expansion of its woodchipping and uranium interests.
"We have had flat earnings for about the past five years, but this will change in 1997/98, when we expect a substantial lift," Anderson said.
"This is because of the company's new projects coming onstream," he said. He added the results for the three months to September 30, 1996 would be released at the end of November.
Anderson said the new projects included its 25 percent interest in the Alumbrera copper/gold project in Argentina, which is scheduled to start prodcution by August 1997.

He said the contribution from its Northparkes copper/gold mine in New South wales should increase in 1997/98, as should expansion of North's uranium interests through its 68 percent owned Energy Resources Australia Ltd (ERA).
ERA said in June it would expand its Ranger mine in the Northern Territory. ERA has also said recently its production outlook was the brightest in 15 years.
North reported a net profit of A$111.89 million in the year to June 30, 1996, compared with A$116.37 million a year earlier.
At 11.55 a.m (0055 GMT), North shares were three cents down at A$3.57.
